geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the isolated cantilever with a split-wing mass to preserve a strong primary body while opening a clear public seam at ground level.
Split along the frontage-compliant axis so the void can register as an access-facing threshold.
Introduce a measured gap to create a usable public void rather than a superficial notch.
Keep the upper body connected so the form retains hierarchy and one clear dominant mass.
Add a courtyard macro wrapped around the dominant mass to produce a true public room at the ground edge.
Keep the courtyard substantial enough to be experienced as neighborhood public space.
Orient the court opening to the program-frame access side so the ground threshold responds to the verified frontage.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the pure cantilever gesture with a split-wing organization so the mass can preserve one dominant anchor while creating a clearer public threshold toward the access edge.
Bring the break earlier so the ground-support relationship becomes more legible and the entry void reads at the frontage.
Add a new public void node to carve a usable court linked to the verified access edge instead of a token notch.
Size the court as an actual usable neighborhood room rather than a decorative subtraction.
Align the new void to the program frame access side so the frontage becomes public and legible.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single object across views, so it avoids outright fragmentation, but it reads as a compact stepped/cantilevered mass with only a small, semantically weak void response. The dominant gesture is visible and the solid remains intact across views, yet the form does not convincingly register the program's required active ground edge or clear public threshold at the verified access side. The blue frontage edge is adjacent, but the mass does not open legibly toward it; the void is too minor and too abstract to count as a usable neighborhood court or terrace. The silhouette is acceptable as a massing idea, but the section language is still more sculptural than programmatic. Compared with the similar references, it resonates only partially with courtyard/commercial neighborhood precedents and misses their clearer public room logic. As a neighborhood living / mixed-use brief, it is plausible in volume but not yet program-fit because the ground/public relation and section logic are underdeveloped.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more open and atmospheric; candidate is much more sealed and heavy, with weaker ground threshold.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact commercial massing with a legible public edge and a carved-in courtyard/patio logic that supports neighborhood occupancy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate lacks the same generosity and clarity of the court; its subtraction reads more as a notch than a public room.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A courtyard-facing perimeter mass can support a neighborhood program when the void is clearly usable and linked to the public edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate over-relies on a compact stacked body without the same direct frontage readability.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise commercial massing can stay calm while using a clear opening and simple section to activate the street.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is more tower-like and programmatically distant; only the ground-to-upper contrast is loosely transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A grounded base and a more articulated upper mass can preserve hierarchy while creating public urban presence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual only; typology and sectional behavior are mismatched to neighborhood living and should not be copied.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A bridge-like connector can create a public passage and continuous pedestrian experience.

warnings: Visible mass is coherent but the public void is too small to satisfy the active threshold requirement.
The frontage response is semantically weak: no legible entry seam, undercut, or court opens to the verified access edge.
Section reads as stacked/canted sculpture more than as neighborhood living with active ground and calm upper massing.
